name: okf-drift
description: Project memory as an OKF v0.2 bundle in which the code is the source of truth: /okf-setup scaffolds a fixed layout (project/{state,stack,setup,conventions}, architecture/, one concept per decision and per playbook) that validates --strict from the first commit, with code paths listed in code_refs; /okf-write records into it under one writing rule (a concept holds what the code does not say — why, invariants, traps, conventions, where to look — and never restates signatures, defaults, steps or numbers), writing each change to the branch's log entry (okf-log.sh add; okf-tidy.sh keeps index rows and dates); /okf-read recalls through okf-recall.sh, giving every hit its lifecycle status and review date and, when commits touched its code_refs after the concept's last commit, a change hint naming them — informative only: a concept found wrong while relied on is fixed as an ordinary edit (read-repair); /okf-migrate moves an older bundle to the split log layout and off drift (drift.lock deleted, CI and CLAUDE.md sections updated, concepts reviewed against the writing rule). The model-invocable okf-runtime skill runs the pinned gate and recall without consumer scripts; the four named skills remain manual. Ships the six-step gate, which fails while a drift.lock is left, and a standalone verified CI bootstrap. A `wiki` profile (.okf-profile) serves knowledge bases that describe no code: no snapshot or code_refs demanded, every structural check kept.
